# VOLTTRON Installer – AI Guide

- Architecture: Reflex app with FastAPI backend mounted in [volttron_installer/volttron_installer.py](volttron_installer/volttron_installer.py); backend APIs initialize via [volttron_installer/backend/__init__.py](volttron_installer/backend/__init__.py) and share the same app instance.
- Frontend patterns: stateful flows use large `rx.State` subclasses in [volttron_installer/state.py](volttron_installer/state.py) (platforms, tools, navigation). State methods call thin API wrappers in [volttron_installer/thin_endpoint_wrappers](volttron_installer/thin_endpoint_wrappers) to hit backend routes; keep async events `@rx.event(background=True)` when making network calls to avoid blocking the UI.
- Styling/layout: global styles live in [volttron_installer/styles](volttron_installer/styles); pages are under [volttron_installer/pages](volttron_installer/pages) (home, platform builder, BACnet scan). New pages should compose existing components under [volttron_installer/components](volttron_installer/components) instead of recreating controls.
- Settings and env: `.env`/`dev.env` must define `VI_APP_NAME`, `VI_SECRET_KEY`, `VI_UPLOAD_DIR`, `VI_DATA_DIR`, `API_URL`, `BACKEND_PORT`, `FRONTEND_PORT`, `TOOL_PROXY_URL` as shown in [dev.env](dev.env). `rxconfig.py` loads one of these files at startup and passes ports/api_url into Reflex.
- Data storage: user data lives under `VI_DATA_DIR` (default `~/.volttron_installer_data`); Ansible inventory is `inventory.yml` managed by [volttron_installer/backend/services/inventory_service.py](volttron_installer/backend/services/inventory_service.py). Platform definitions are YAML per instance in that directory via [volttron_installer/backend/services/platform_service.py](volttron_installer/backend/services/platform_service.py).
- Backend API: main router is [volttron_installer/backend/endpoints.py](volttron_installer/backend/endpoints.py). It exposes platform CRUD, host inventory CRUD, deployment/status operations (Ansible + SSH), task utilities, tool lifecycle, and BACnet scan proxy routes. Pydantic models and agent catalog defaults are in [volttron_installer/backend/models.py](volttron_installer/backend/models.py).
- Ansible integration: [volttron_installer/backend/services/ansible_service.py](volttron_installer/backend/services/ansible_service.py) runs collection playbooks (prefixed `volttron.deployment.*`) or raw SSH commands. Inventory must contain the host instance name; `ignore_host_keys` is handled by extra vars. Deployment steps include venv setup, pip installs, vctl status checks, and process cleanup.
- Tool lifecycle: external tools (e.g., BACnet scan API) are launched on-demand with [volttron_installer/backend/tool_manager.py](volttron_installer/backend/tool_manager.py); proxies expose them under `/tool_proxy/{tool}/{path}` via [volttron_installer/backend/tool_router.py](volttron_installer/backend/tool_router.py). Frontend configs live in `ToolState.tool_configs` in [volttron_installer/state.py](volttron_installer/state.py); add new tools there and supply `ToolRequest` entries.
- BACnet scan integration: the BACnet scanner service lives in sibling repo `../eclipse-bacnet-scan-tool` and is started through the tool manager; results are modeled in `bacnet_scan_api.models` and used by BACnet UI/state in [volttron_installer/pages/bacnet_scan.py](volttron_installer/pages/bacnet_scan.py).
- Required sibling repos: this repo expects `../eclipse-bacnet-scan-tool`, `../lib-protocol-proxy-fixed`, and `../lib-protocol-proxy-bacnet-fixed` present (see [README.md](README.md)); Pixi tasks install them in editable mode.
- Dev workflow (Pixi): run `pixi run dev` for first-time install + serve, `pixi run run` to serve with existing deps, `pixi run test` for pytest, `pixi run install-deps` to force reinstall. Pixi pins Python 3.10 and installs the VOLTTRON Ansible collection.
- Manual workflow: if not using Pixi, create a 3.10 venv, `pip install -e ../lib-protocol-proxy-fixed -e ../lib-protocol-proxy-bacnet-fixed -e ../eclipse-bacnet-scan-tool`, then `pip install -r requirements.txt -e .` and run `reflex run`.
- Backing services: Ansible collection `volttron-ansible` must be installed (Pixi task handles it). SSH key auth between controller and hosts is assumed; host definitions set `ansible_user`, `ansible_host`, optional proxies, and venv/home paths.
- Testing: pytest config in [pyproject.toml](pyproject.toml) sets `tests/` root. Tests exist under [tests/backend](tests/backend); keep new tests asynchronous-aware (`asyncio_mode=auto`).
- Common pitfalls: ensure only one VOLTTRON_HOME per instance, keep inventory instance names unique, and do not block the Reflex event loop with long Ansible/SSH calls—run them via background events or backend tasks.
- When adding backend routes: put them in `endpoints.py`, use services for filesystem or Ansible I/O instead of direct writes, and extend Pydantic models in `backend/models.py` rather than ad-hoc dicts. Keep responses serializable for the Reflex client.
- Deployment data model: `PlatformDefinition` pairs a `HostEntry` id with `PlatformConfig` and an `agents` dict of `AgentDefinition`. Defaults for common agents and config store templates live in `AgentCatalog` within `backend/models.py`.
- Tool cleanup: shutdown hooks call `ToolManager.stop_all_tools()` in the app lifespan; if you spawn processes, register them there or track in `_tool_processes` to avoid orphaned services.
